rows.author: J077;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION WORKERS IN ALL BARANGAYS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes that there shall be at least one   (1) barangay agricultural extension worker (BAEW) with areas devoted to farming,   raising of animals, and fishing with SG equivalent to Agricultural Technician   1 or Aquacultural Technician 1.
    
Proposes that the BAEW in barangays without any farming or fishing activities to assist and encourage urban gardening to support community-based and household-based food production using rooftops, small spaces, and other vacant spaces.
   
Proposes for BAEW´s accreditation and qualifications; duties and responsibilities; incentives and benefits including training, education, and career enrichment programs such as special training programs on agriculture entrepreneurship (marketing and value chain approach,   disaster response and preparedness, etc.); and crash courses related to communal irrigation system; climate-smart agriculture; water management,   climate-resilient crop varieties; livestock; climate-resilient fisheries;   integrated multi-trophic aquaculture systems; pasturing in livestock and aquaculture feeding; and early warning system.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2024-02-21

rows.author: J118;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FINANCING SYSTEM FOR AGRICULTURE AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10000 OR "THE AGRI-AGRA REFORM CREDIT ACT OF 2009"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the issue regarding our poor farmers and those supposed target beneficiaries´ inadequate access to government-directed credit programs and their dependence on informal lenders who charge unreasonable interest rates. 
     
Seeks to institutionalize the zero interest loans and well-assessed and accepted loan maturity dates for payment that shall be in accordance with the farmer´s cash flows and the gestation and harvest period of the agricultural produce/activity/project being financed.   
 
Tasks the Land Bank of the Phils. (LBP) and the Development Bank of the Phils. (DBP) to continue to promote savings and credit in rural areas by offering affordable and accessible deposit products such as the basic deposit account for deposits and low to no interest rates for loans.
     
Provides that lending cooperatives,   microfinance institutions, retail banks, and rural and thrift banks shall apply minimum to zero interest rates for wholesale loans obtained from government banks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2024-02-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF LOCAL STUDIES CENTERS IN STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES THROUGHOUT THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to ensure the preservation of our fellowmen´s interest in our local cultural heritage through establishing centers that aim to become pivotal in researching, documenting, conserving, and promoting the country´s rich cultural heritage, specifically at the grassroots level.
   
Seeks to harness the academic and scientific capabilities of SUCs in exploring and preserving the Philippines´ history and culture to serve as leverage to become platforms for systematic study of local heritage.   
 
Proposes to provide copies of each publication for deposit at the Historical Data Bank of the National   Historical Commission of the Phils. (NHCP), the National Library of the   Phils., and the University of the Phils. Diliman Filipiniana Library.
   

   
Tasks the DFA to purchase and   disseminate copies of publications to all Sentro Rizal cultural centers in   foreign service posts

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY HUBS NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen Filipinos' information and technology literacy to create a more inclusive digital economy and to accelerate digital transformation in the Phil. Economy, increase job opportunities and foster a competitive ICT sector.

Refers Public Telecommunications Entity (PTE) to any person, natural or juridical, government or privately engaged in providing telecommunications services to the public for compensation.

Defines ICT HUB as a location where a PTE may provide ICT services with at least the minimum internet speed required by the NTC.Â  Such services may include telecommunication services, broadband and convergence services, business processing, and data management.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING CRITICAL MEDICAL PRODUCTS, ESSENTIAL GOODS, INPUTS, RAW MATERIALS, AND EQUIPMENT FROM TAXES, DUTIES, AND OTHER FEES DURING PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES
rows.abstract:
Refers critical medical products to vaccines and other necessary medicines to contain Public Health Emergencies; Also defines Essential goods to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and supplies . . . surgical equipment and supplies; laboratory equipment and its reagents; medical equipment and devices; . . . and such other supplies or equipment as may be determined by the DOH and other relevant government agencies; . . .
Enumerates the causes of public health emergencies - bioterrorism, the appearance of a novel or infectious agent or biological toxin, chemical/nuclear/radioactive materials attack, or accidental release.

Proposes for the following exemptions:Â  VAT, Customs Duties, and Other Fees for Private Firms/NGAs, or LGUs; Donor´s Tax and Other Fees for Private Firms, NGAs, or LGUs; Export Requirements.Â  Proposes to allow expenses incurred by private firms as tax deductions from gross income.

rows.author: K122;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK ON RESILIENT HOUSING AND HUMAN SETTLEMENTS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes a national framework that will lay out a concrete plan whenever the country is adversely affected by national disasters and effects of climate change, and which shall serve as the basis for a mechanism for post-disaster housing and settlements rehabilitation and resiliency planning and response at all levels.

Seeks to complement the provisions in Sec.5, I-(e) of R.A. No.11201 which is a mandate to the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) to formulate a framework . . . by identifying its components including a National Housing Resilient Agenda and priorities; a National Post-Disaster Housing Recovery Strategy and Rules and Guidelines for Rehabilitation, Reconstruction, and Relocation; Investment and Financing Requirements; and Institutional Arrangements, among others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT”¯ FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7836, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE TEACHERS PROFESSIONALIZATION ACT OF 1994” AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9293
rows.title_short: Further Amending Republic Act No. 7836, Otherwise Known As The “ Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act Of 1994” As Amended By Republic Act No. 9293
rows.abstract:
Seeks to widen the nomination for the members of the Board of Professional Teachers by including the Teachers Education Council (TEC), Department of Education (DepEd), accredited association of public and private schools and school administrators, Commission on Higher Education (CHED), Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) and accredited association of teachers.
Mandates the Professional Regulatory Commission (PRC) to issue the appropriate rules to govern the practice of Members of the Board to ensure that no conflict of interest shall arise in their functions related to the conduct of the licensure examination and release of the results.
Recognizes the probationary employment in private basic education schools pursuant to DOLE-DECS-CHED-TESDA Order No. 1 series of 1986 to teach prior to acquiring the necessary certificate and license subject to certain conditions.
Proposes additional academic qualification for applicants who will take the licensure examinations for teachers and the requirement of a refresher course for those who have failed to pass the licensure examination for three times.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the supervisory and regulatory role of the government in all public and private higher education institutions (HEIs) taking into consideration the complementarity of the public and private sectors in education, and guarantee their institutional academic freedom.
Mandates the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and other relevant government regulatory agencies to exercise reasonable supervision and regulation of all higher education institutions which includes imposing reasonable requirements, setting conditions, prescribing restrictions, and ensuring compliance.
Fixes the criteria for the establishment of HEIs and sets the minimum requirements for their course offering.
Grants incentives for high standards of quality for all HEIs that consistently demonstrate and adhere to standards of excellence.
